subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The FDA classifies a food as "organic" only if it contains at least 95% organically produced ingredients.
• The European Union's organic certification doesn't require a specific percentage threshold.
• Under EU standards, many products with 70-94% organic ingredients can be labeled organic.
• Under FDA standards, those same products would be labeled "made with organic ingredients" rather than organic.
prompt: The student wants to contrast the FDA's definition of organic food with the European Union's. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The FDA's definition of organic food—containing at least 95% organically produced ingredients—is more restrictive than the European Union's, which doesn't require a specific percentage threshold.
choices.B: The European Union, which doesn't require a specific percentage threshold for organic certification, allows many products with varying organic content to be labeled organic.
choices.C: Because its definition of organic food is different from the FDA's, it is unclear what standards the European Union actually uses for organic certification.
choices.D: According to the FDA's definition of organic—containing at least 95% organically produced ingredients—many EU-certified organic products would be labeled differently in the US.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence contrasts the FDA's definition of organic food with the European Union's, explaining that the FDA's definition (which requires a specific percentage) is more restrictive than the EU's definition (which doesn't).
